subject: 白居寺 · 吉祥多门塔（十万佛塔）全貌
name: 白居寺吉祥多门塔
sub: 十万佛塔全貌 · 九层塔寺合一
yearNote: 《汉藏史集》记江孜法王饶丹贡桑帕1427年（明宣德二年）为十万佛像吉祥多门塔奠基，至1436年完成泥塑、壁画与装饰（人民网《白居寺建筑与壁画艺术》引）；中文维基与中国西藏网另记塔始建于1414年、历时十年，英文维基记1427–1437年。白居寺措钦大殿早于塔，寺1418年动工。年表取1427年奠基，标约略。
place: 西藏 · 日喀则 · 江孜
coordinate_source: Wikidata Q1785045（白居寺 Palcho Monastery）P625 坐标 28.923931, 89.595324，寺院本体近似坐标，非本项目测绘；地图显示点复用本批新建的 xz_gyantse（与 xz_gyantse_dzong 共用）。
lede: 1427年，江孜法王饶丹贡桑帕为十万佛像吉祥多门塔奠基，约十年后塑绘装饰齐备。四面二十角的塔座层层收缩，托起圆形塔瓶、方形塔颈与鎏金十三天；塔内开108道门、设77间佛殿，壁画塑像以万计，寺中有塔、塔中有寺，是后藏塔寺合一的典范。
facts: 年代：《汉藏史集》记饶丹贡桑帕于1427年奠基，至1436年完成泥塑壁画；另有1414年始建之说。1996年随白居寺列第四批国保。
形制：全塔九层、通高42.4米（一说32米余），塔座呈四面二十角、底边约40米，塔瓶直径20米，上承十三法轮与伞状鎏金宝盖。
塔寺合一：开108道门、设77间佛殿，一至四层每层16或20间，塔瓶4间；塔内绘塑佛像27529身，故称“十万佛塔”。
caption: 白居寺吉祥多门塔 · 十万佛塔全貌
明 · 1427–1436
structure_checkpoints: 塔瓶以下自下而上共五道赭红色檐带：最下为高大的白色塔基，檐下绕一圈蓝地彩绘宝相花带；其上四层佛殿塔座逐层收缩，每层檐口为短赭红檐，檐下饰彩绘菱形图案带与一排白点；各层转角呈台阶状内折（四面二十角），正面轮廓为阶梯金字塔，白墙上只开零星小方窗。
塔瓶：塔座之上为白色圆柱形塔瓶，正面有一座彩绘拱形龛门（门楣上绘慧眼）；瓶顶出一圈宽阔的深色圆形飞檐，檐下有斗栱。
塔颈（横斗）：方形，四面彩绘花纹，正面绘一双大慧眼；其上为鎏金锥形十三天，可数13道水平环。
塔顶：十三天之上为带镂空栏杆和垂帘的伞状鎏金宝盖，顶立鎏金宝瓶与尖顶；宝盖以四根斜拉索固定到塔瓶飞檐（线稿可省略拉索）。
主图自东南斜向拍摄、前景有经幡柱，补充图自南偏东仰拍、塔瓶有维修脚手架；塔体四面对称，绘正面时按对称补全，去除经幡柱、脚手架、转经筒廊、旁侧寺院建筑与山顶宗山城墙。
material_observations: 塔身为石砌白色抹灰；各层檐口赭红色，檐下彩绘菱形纹与蓝、绿、金色图案带，白点饰；塔基彩绘带以蓝色为地；塔瓶白色，龛门彩绘蓝、红、金；塔瓶飞檐深褐色；十三天与宝盖鎏金铜，宝盖垂饰红蓝彩绘；塔前地面为灰色石板。
author: Antoine Taveneaux

additional_sources.author: Gerd Eichmann
additional_sources.role: 南偏东仰视，核对塔瓶、塔颈慧眼、十三天与宝盖的层次（塔瓶部分有脚手架）

source_note: 主图为 Antoine Taveneaux 2009 年自东南方向拍摄的吉祥多门塔全景（CC BY-SA 3.0），能数清塔瓶以下五道檐带、塔瓶飞檐、十三天与宝盖；补充图为 Gerd Eichmann 2014 年 5 月仰拍（CC BY-SA 4.0），用于核对塔颈慧眼与宝盖栏杆细节。两图均为斜向，线稿按四面对称绘正面；前景经幡柱、脚手架、人物与周边建筑去除。
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK line drawing on a perfectly flat opaque PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF) background. Use confident fine contours and a few finer internal structural lines. All unmarked surfaces inside and outside the drawing remain pure white; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, broad grey shading, crosshatching, pencil grain, paper texture, gradient, color, gold, halo, cast shadow or checkerboard. The white canvas will be removed later by a script; draw only the ink strokes and keep all other regions uniformly white.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Wide compositions: landscape 1536×1024, entire building occupies about 82% of canvas width, roof/apex and base uncut, balanced breathing room. Tall pagodas: portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 82% of height, centred with equal side margins, apex and base uncut.

SUBJECT: the Kumbum (Palcho Chörten, 吉祥多门塔 / 十万佛塔) of Palcho Monastery, Gyantse, Tibet, a nine-storey stepped stupa-temple, drawn as a straight-on frontal elevation reconstructed from two oblique photos (Image 2: 2009 view from the south-east with a prayer-flag pole in front; Image 3: 2014 upward view with scaffolding around the dome). The stupa is symmetrical on all four sides; draw ONE face straight on. From bottom to top: (1) a tall white plinth with a continuous painted frieze band under a plain cornice; (2) FOUR receding white terraces above it, each with a short red-brown cornice over a frieze of diamond panels and a row of dots, each terrace indented at the corners in steps so the outline is a stepped pyramid; count exactly FIVE cornice lines below the dome (plinth plus four terraces); only a few tiny square windows on the white walls; (3) a plain cylindrical white dome with one arched, ornately framed niche door on its face, crowned by a wide round projecting eave on bracket sets; (4) a square harmika block with a pair of large painted eyes on the face; (5) a tall gilded conical spire of THIRTEEN horizontal rings; (6) a round gilded canopy with a lattice balustrade and hanging fringe (omit the guy-wires); (7) a gilded vase-and-jewel finial. The whole stupa is nearly as wide as it is tall: make it occupy about 62% of the canvas height so that its full base width fits with clear side margins; apex and base uncut. Remove the prayer-flag poles, scaffolding, people, prayer-wheel gallery, adjacent monastery buildings, the hilltop fortress wall and the sky.
Orientation: portrait 1024×1536.
